finding: A real local continuation-value approximation gap survives the existing chain/first-offer scores: root28 is corrected by ordinary executable-continuation rollout. Across the entire fixed 72-root cohort, that standard improvement still loses to the fixed rolling-nominal policy in average travel loss and costs more CPU. No new structural algorithm is justified by this panel.
negative_evidence: The same combined policy with received messages loses 20.652778 seconds on average relative to its no-message arm, from three negative realizations. This is not proof that information is harmful or that the forecast model is wrong; it motivates checking the declared message model before adding planning depth.
retained: Source and message timestamp inventory, complete eligibility denominator, selected natural cases
Persistent message-aware posterior and common service-notice planning masks
All original six policies, both information arms, positive/negative action receipts
Four fixed conditional references including unresolved projection mass
Standard conditional rollout as an additional benchmark, not a novel method
Full CPU accounting and the preserved root28 timing upper bound
limitations: Six development dates and a fixed 16-station time-window/menu; not independent confirmation or the full network
Forecast bandwidth is declared from route training spread, not calibrated forecast-error noise
Future message revisions are not generated; conditional simulations hold the received snapshot fixed
Logical-clock physical quality is separate from real-time computation feasibility
No claim that every stronger existing policy has been exhausted or that information-action coupling is impossible
next_step: Retain this panel and its strong frontier.
